messages:
matt: :rotating_light: Pager Duty triggered - high error rate for internal SRV resolution in us-west-2a. Seeing lots of SERVFAIL from CoreDNS clusters. Root TS: 2501234567
oncall-bot: @sasha is on-call (primary). Incident channel created.
pagerduty-bot: Triggered: SRV-LOOKUP-ERRORS-USW2 (SEV2) — escalated to on-call. Link: https://pd.example/INC12345
sasha: Got it, I'm on the call. Observing elevated latency and some timeouts in services that rely on consul SRV queries. Running quick dig against cluster: `dig +short SRV _api._tcp.service.consul @10.0.8.15` returns no records, RCODE=SERVFAIL.
evan: I can confirm from telemetry: CoreDNS pod CPU spikes to 95% and there's increased retries from app clients. Graphs show query rate up 6x from normal, and error rate for SRV up ~30%.
anya: Any recent deploys in us-west-2 that could have changed CoreDNS/consul config?
matt: No deploys to coredns this morning. We did push an autoscaler change in the region earlier but not to DNS.
sasha: Pulling CoreDNS logs now — hitting `panic` in plugin chain? Logs show repeated `kubernetes: no endpoints` then `dns: upstream read error: read udp ...: i/o timeout`.
katy: Adding network team — could be egress or route issue to consul servers? cc @eng-sre
eng-sre: Noted. I'll check node network path and any peering changes. Last peering churn was 4h ago but should be stable.
evan: Also seeing 5xx errors for user facing endpoints that use SRV discovery to select backend. Customers in us-west reported increased 502s over the last 10 minutes.
sasha: Immediate mitigation plan: 1) Reduce query volume by enabling client-side caching TTL override temporarily; 2) Scale coredns replicas; 3) Failover traffic to us-west-2b via routing policy for non-latency-sensitive customer tiers. Who can run scale commands?
matt: I can scale coredns replicas. Which kube cluster? `cluster-usw2-dns`?
sasha: Yes. Run `kubectl -n kube-system scale deployment coredns --replicas=6 --context=usw2` (we're at 3 replicas).
matt: Running now...
matt: kubectl output: `deployment.apps/coredns scaled` — pods spinning up.
evan: Noted. Meanwhile I'm going to flip client retries to 2 and increase backoff to 500ms in the routing proxy config for internal clients. That should dampen QPS to DNS.
anya: I'm going to push a short lived iptables rule on coredns nodes to drop stale UDP fragments? Wait, not comfortable with that. Alternative: route consul SRV lookups to the alternate consul aggregator endpoint in the other AZ.
eng-sre: I see a partial egress path degradation from us-west-2a to our consul leaders in us-west-2b; some packets dropped, leading to timeouts to upstream. BGP paths show flapping on fabric switch usw2a-agg3. Network ops is investigating.
katy: Network ops reports a hardware flapping on agg3. They are rerouting flow but convergence may take a couple minutes and cause intermittent failures. Recommendation: move control-plane traffic off agg3 by adding policy route for consul endpoints to use secondary path.
sasha: Ok, executable steps: 1) scale coredns (in progress). 2) set client-side cache override in envoy to cache SRV for 30s temporarily. 3) add fallback in CoreDNS to forward to consul aggregator in us-west-2b for SRV queries. Evan, can you change envoy config? Anya, can you make CoreDNS patch? eng-sre, coordinate network path patch.
evan: Patching envoy route now - updating config map and triggering rolling restart for proxy pods in service mesh: `kubectl -n mesh rollout restart deploy/proxy`.
anya: Creating a Corefile patch, adding a `forward` block specifically for `_svc._tcp.service.consul` pointing at 10.0.9.20 (usw2b aggregator):
``nsvc.consul:53 {
    forward . 10.0.9.20
}
```
Applying patch with `kubectl -n kube-system patch configmap coredns --patch ...`
anya: Patch applied. CoreDNS pods reloaded the config.
matt: New coredns pods are ready: 3 -> 6 replicas.
evan: Envoy restart completed. Clients should now cache SRV for 30s. Telemetry shows QPS to coredns falling ~40%.
eng-sre: Network ops confirms the agg3 interface is still flapping, but traffic now rerouted. We're seeing packet loss drop from ~8% to ~1%.
sasha: Monitoring for customer impact and errors. Requesting SRE to keep on-call engaged for 30 minutes post mitigation.
katy: Quick customer impact note: Internal monitoring indicates ~12% of requests in us-west for customers with strict AZ affinity experienced 502s for ~8-12 minutes. No global outage. We should prepare a brief message for affected customers.
matt: I can draft a status note: keep it factual, mention mitigation and that we're still investigating root cause with the network vendor.
anya: Oncall handoff: @sasha hands to @evan in 25 minutes unless further escalations. Marking for postmortem.
oncall-bot: Handoff recorded: sasha -> evan at 2501234730
pagerduty-bot: Alert resolved (partial mitigation) — will stay open for follow-up monitoring.
evan: Logging summary for postmortem: timeline, mitigations (scale coredns, client cache, forward to aggregator, routing change), customer impact estimate (12% of requests for small subset), next steps (replace agg3 NIC, add routing policy for control-plane redundancy, improve client fallback to use HTTP failover when SRV fails).
sasha: Thanks everyone. I'll keep channel open for any new symptoms. If network ops confirms hardware fix, we'll coordinate rolling revert of temp config (remove forward and reduce cache). For now keep elevated logging for SRV queries.
katy: Notifying customer success to prepare messages. @matt please share outage window and affected AZ list.
matt: Sending note to CS: impacted AZ: us-west-2a, approx window 16:03-16:15 PT, approximate % traffic impacted 12% for AZ-affinitized customers.
eng-sre: Filed incident ticket INC-2501234567 in tracker for full postmortem.
anya: Adding config snippets to incident artifacts and saving CoreDNS logs to S3: s3://redwood-incident-logs/INC-2501234567/coredns.log
sasha: Closing out on-call handoff. Thanks team.
oncall-bot: Channel archived in 2h unless manually kept open.
